questions.question: Question 3
questions.solution_html:
• Support entrepreneurship through loans, underwriting, and guarantees.
  • 4a. Explain how a Startup Ecosystem supports entrepreneurship.
  • The startup ecosystem includes incubators, accelerators, investors, mentors, and government
  • policies that promote innovation and growth.It provides access to funding, networking, training
  • and infrastructure, enabling startups to scale efficiently.
  • OR
  • 4b. Discuss the key features of the Stand-Up India Scheme.
  • Launched in 2016 to promote entrepreneurship among women and SC/ST communities.
  • Provides bank loans between ₹10 lakh–₹1 crore for setting up new enterprises.
  • Aims for inclusive economic growth by empowering underrepresented groups.
  • 5a. Explain Startup India Policy.
  • The Start-up India Policy, launched by the Government of India on January 16, 2016, is a
  • flagship initiative aimed at building a strong ecosystem that nurtures innovation and
  • entrepreneurship.This program offers benefits such as mentoring and networking opportunities
  • tax exemptions, easier compliance, funding support, and incubation assistance.
  • OR
  • 5b. List any four indicators of Ease of Doing Business. (Any other relevant points may be
  • considered and given marks.)
  • Access to electricity.
  • Reserve Company Name

questions.question: Question 4
questions.solution_html:
• Registering property.
  • Short Essay
  • A choice between two options for each question, answer three short essay questions, one from
  • each pair
  • 6a. Why is financial feasibility considered the most critical study?
  • It assesses the financial viability of a business idea by estimating costs, revenues, and
  • profitability.
  • It helps determine whether the venture can sustain and generate adequate returns.Financial
  • feasibility study also prevents losses by forecasting funding needs and break-even points.
  • OR
  • 6b. Explain key methods used to validate a business idea. (Any other relevant points may be
  • considered and given marks.)
  • Concept testing - presenting the product concept symbolically to target customers and get their
  • reaction. The aim is to assess whether the idea is understandable, appealing and useful.
  • Customer Validation - involves creating a Minimum Viable Product (MVP), a basic yet
  • functional version of the product to test the early users. The goal is to gather direct feedback
  • through interviews, surveys and product usage and use it to enhance the idea.
  • Pilot Testing or Test Marketing - launching the final business model or product on a small scale
  • to get an impression from the market and this helps the business to improve before launching it
  • to a larger market.
  • 7a. Why is a business plan referred to as the “roadmap” of a business? (Any other relevant points
  • may be considered and given marks.)
  • Business plan is a written document describing all relevant internal and external elements and
  • strategies for establishing and operating a new venture. It contains the operational and financial
  • plan of a business, and details how its objectives will be achieved. A business plan is often an
  • integration of functional plans such as marketing, finance, manufacturing, and human resources.
  • It guides decision-making and helps monitor progress toward objectives.
  • OR
  • 7b. Briefly explain SWOT Analysis.
  • SWOT stands for Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats.
  • It is a strategic planning tool used to assess internal capabilities and external challenges of a firm.
  • Internal Factors
  • ● Strengths – Competitive advantages and capabilities of the firm.
  • ● Weaknesses – Limitations or gaps in resources or operations.
  • External Factors
  • ● Opportunities – Market trends or changes beneficial for growth of the firm.
  • ● Threats – External risks that may harm the business.
  • 8a. Define Fabian entrepreneurs and explain their characteristics.
  • Fabian entrepreneurs are cautious and skeptical individuals who adopt innovations only when it
  • is inevitable. They prefer steady, moderate growth over rapid expansion.(2 mark)
  • Characteristics (3 mark)
  • ● Accept and stick to traditional methods of business.
  • ● Often involved in family-owned businesses.
  • ● Display carefulness and reluctance to change.
  • ● Operate with a clear, strict, and basic strategy.
  • ● May be seen as unambitious or conservative in business expansion.
  • OR
  • 8b. Discuss any four environmental barriers that affect entrepreneurship. (Any other relevant
  • points may be considered and given marks.)
  • ● Financial constraints - Limited access to loans, investment, or seed capital.
  • ● Regulatory & bureaucratic hurdles - Complicated licensing, taxation, and compliance
  • processes.
  • ● Lack of infrastructure facilities - Poor transportation, electricity, internet, and
  • communication.
  • ● Limited access to resources - Raw materials, skilled labour, or advanced technology are
  • scarce.
  • ● Unsupportive Business environment - Weak support from policymakers, industry bodies
  • or finance system.
  • ● Cultural & social barriers - In some societies, entrepreneurship is not respected.
  • ● Intense competition
  • Long Essay
  • A choice between two options for each question, answer one long essay questions, one from each
  • pair
  • (Any other relevant points may be considered and given marks.)
  • 9a. Renewable energy startup and its contribution to economic and social development.
  • Economic contribution: Generates employment, attracts investment, reduces energy import costs
  • and promotes local industries. (5 mark)
  • Social contribution: Empowers rural youth, ensures energy access, promotes environmental
  • sustainability, and improves living standards. (5 mark)
  • (b) Discuss broader role of entrepreneurs in sustainable and inclusive growth.
  • Entrepreneurs create eco-friendly solutions, promote rural development, and encourage green
  • innovation. (5 mark)
  • Inclusive entrepreneurship reduces inequality and ensures balanced regional growth. (5 mark)
  • OR
  • 9b. (a) Explain how the women’s eco-friendly bag initiative reflects social entrepreneurship. (10
  • marks)
  • ● Focus on solving a social problem (plastic waste).
  • ● Generates employment for rural women.
  • ● Prioritizes community welfare and environmental sustainability over profit.
  • (b) Describe how Priya’s contribution demonstrates intrapreneurship and ts significance to the
  • company. (5 mark)
  • ● She innovated within an organization, developed a recycling process, and reduced
  • costs.
  • ● Her actions improved efficiency and strengthened the company’s sustainability
  • reputation.
  • Significance: (5 mark)
  • ● Encourages employee creativity, enhances competitiveness, and supports organizational
  • innovation.
  • Compulsory Case Study
  • 10a. Private limited company registration process and non-compliance effects.
  • Formalities before starting operations (14 mark)–(2 mark)for each step)
  • Draft and File MOA & AOA
  • • MOA (Memorandum of Association) – defines company objectives, scope, and subscribers.
  • •AOA (Articles of Association) – governs internal rules, management, voting rights, and
  • meetings.
  • • Filed electronically using e-MOA & e-AOA

  • Legal penalties, cancellation of registration, loss of credibility, and restrictions on business
  • expansion.
